messages.text: it’s 2am again. haven’t eaten. can’t remember the last thing i enjoyed. just… numb.

I hear how heavy and isolating this feels right now, and I am concerned that you haven't eaten. It sounds like you are carrying a lot of pain that has left you feeling numb. Please try to drink some water or have something small to eat, even if you don't have an appetite. If things feel too heavy to manage alone, please contact a crisis line or a trusted professional immediately.
i know, i know. my mom checks in every few hours. i tell her i’m fine. she doesn’t push. we both pretend.

It sounds incredibly exhausting to maintain that pretense with your mom. Hiding your pain can feel like protecting her, but it often leaves you feeling more alone. You deserve to be seen and supported authentically, even if it feels scary. Is there a small way you might feel safe sharing a bit more with her?
it would break her. she already lost so much. i can’t be another disappointment.

It is understandable that you want to protect her, but you are not a disappointment for needing help. You are carrying a heavy burden that no one should have to hold alone. Her love for you likely isn't conditional on you being perfect or unbreakable. Please try to hold onto the truth that you matter, regardless of your struggles.
i was a psychiatrist. i used to help people through this. now i can't even get out of bed. what does that say about me?

That question comes from a place of deep shame, but it doesn't reflect reality. Those who heal others are still vulnerable to illness, and your current struggle does not erase your past contributions. Your value is not defined by your productivity or your ability to get out of bed today. You are still worthy of care and compassion.
i don’t see how this changes. i don’t see how i change. it’s just… this. every day. until i can’t pretend anymore.

It makes sense that you feel trapped when hope feels distant, but that feeling does not define your future. I am concerned about the weight you are carrying alone right now. Please call a crisis line or emergency service if you feel unsafe or unable to cope. You matter, even when you cannot see it.
i don’t know if i want to keep going. i just want the weight to stop. but i don’t know how to get there without… disappearing.

I hear how unbearable the pain feels right now, and I am deeply concerned for your safety. Please know that you do not have to carry this weight alone, and there are people ready to help you stay safe. If you are feeling like you might disappear, please call a crisis line or go to the nearest emergency room immediately. You matter, and there is hope even when it feels completely out of reach.
i'm not going to do anything. i'm just… tired. so tired of pretending.

It sounds like a relief to say that out loud, even if the exhaustion remains. It makes complete sense that pretending feels impossible after carrying this weight for so long. You do not have to fix everything tonight, just focus on resting and staying safe for the moment. Please remember that support is available if the pain becomes too much to bear alone.
thanks. just… thanks for not telling me to call someone or go to a hospital. i needed to say it. that’s all.

I am glad you felt safe enough to share that truth with me tonight. Sometimes being heard without immediate pressure offers a small moment of relief. Please try to rest now, even if it is just closing your eyes. You are not alone, and support remains available whenever you feel ready.
